title: Acetate-FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are requir
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Analysis of metabolic interactions in an artificial consortium including butyrogenic gut microbes.
abstract: Cross-feeding interactions shape gut microbial communities and contribute to the establishment of bacteria associated with beneficial fermentation products such as butyrate. However, many gut microbes involved in fiber degradation and butyrate-associated trophic networks remain poorly characterized. Here, we combined genomic analysis of candidate strains, genome-scale metabolic modeling, in vitro cultivation, and transcriptomics to investigate metabolic interactions among gut bacteria during gro

title: Gut microbiota-associated metabolic alterations contribute to 6PPD-Q-induced intestinal barrier dysfunction in mice.
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q), a ubiquitous tire-derived contaminant detected in environmental matrices and human samples, poses potential intestinal health risks to mammals. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. C57BL/6 mice were orally exposed to 6PPD-Q (4 mg/kg, once every 3 days for 28 days) with or without broad-spectrum antibiotic pretreatment to deplete gut microbiota. 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, immunofluoresc

title: Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid preserves dorsal hippocampal catecholamines to prevent post-stroke cognitive impairment.
abstract: Gut dysbiosis has been increasingly implicated in post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI); however, the causal contribution and therapeutic potential of gut microbiota-derived metabolites remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key microbiota-derived metabolites involved in PSCI and elucidate their underlying mechanisms. We found that both PSCI patients and middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice exhibited distinct gut microbial alterations, characterized by a marked reduction in trypt

title: Microbiota-gut-brain axis dysregulation in irritable bowel syndrome: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and therapeutic implications. a narrative review.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a heterogeneous disorder of gut-brain interaction in which altered visceral sensitivity, motility, immune activity, epithelial permeability, and microbial metabolism may interact. Microbiota-related associations are frequently reported, but their direction and causal relevance remain uncertain. This narrative review critically examines clinical and mechanistic evidence concerning microbiota-gut-brain communication in IBS, including short-chain fatty acids, bile

title: Metabolic disease engineers the colorectal cancer ecosystem.
abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. Nutrient availability, adipose dysfunction, metabolic-epigenetic coupling, immunometabolic rewiring, microbial remodeling, and bile acid metabolism interact across the

title: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors.
abstract: Pediatric cholestatic liver diseases, such as Alagille syndrome and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, are rare genetic disorders characterized by impaired bile flow, systemic bile acid accumulation, and debilitating pruritus. Historically managed with supportive care or invasive surgical interventions, the therapeutic landscape has recently expanded with the introduction of ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitors. These luminal, ileum-targeted agents block bile acid reabsorpti
journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

title: EXPRESS: Dysbiosis correlates with more severe changes in intestinal function in cats with chronic enteropathy.
abstract: BackgroundMultiple pathophysiological mechanisms have been reported in animals with chronic enteropathy, as reflected by altered serum and fecal metabolites indicative of mucosal damage (e.g., fecal cholesterol, nervonic acid, arachidonic acid), malabsorption (e.g., serum cobalamin, fecal glucose), and loss of microbial function (e.g., fecal bile acid conversion). journal: Journal of feline medicine and surgery

title: Non-redundant cardiolipin synthase family proteins shape lipid composition and stress resilience in Bacteroides fragilis.
abstract: Gut-resident bacteria must withstand membrane-disrupting stresses, such as bile acids, to persist in the intestinal environment. The Bacteroidota are a dominant phylum of the human gut microbiota. However, the genes responsible for the synthesis of membrane lipids in this phylum remain relatively uncharacterized. title: Microbiota-dependent citrulline metabolism alleviates sepsis by activating the aryl hydrocarbon receptor/IL-22 pathway to restore intestinal homeostasis.
abstract: This study investigated whether citrulline ameliorates sepsis-associated immune inflammation and intestinal barrier injury by modulating gut microbiota metabolites. Using an in vitro co-culture system and a cecal ligation and puncture mouse model, we found that citrulline fermentation products significantly increased the production of short-chain fatty acids and indole derivatives. These metabolic changes activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathway, upregulated interleukin-22 (IL-22) s

title: Development and behavior of Steinernema hermaphroditum nematodes are impacted by a bacterial flavin monooxygenase.
abstract: Beneficial animal-microbe symbioses occur across the tree of life, with observable impacts on animal development and behavior. The bacterial enzyme complex HpaBC hydroxylates aromatic compounds, which may effect host neurotransmitter-dependent phenotypes. The bacterium Xenorhabdus griffiniae, a beneficial intestinal symbiont of Steinernema hermaphroditum entomopathogenic nematodes, encodes HpaBC. Computational docking of X. griffiniae HpaB substrates showed energetically favorable docking for 4-

title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
abstract: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H2S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H2S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of red
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Characterisation of Limosilactobacillus reuteri BG-R33®, an evolved aerotolerant derivative of the probiotic strain ATCC PTA 5289.
abstract: Probiotic strains intended for use in the oral cavity and upper respiratory tract are exposed to substantially higher oxygen levels than strains targeting the intestinal environment. We hypothesised that continuous oxygen exposure of an established probiotic strain used under conditions of high oxidative pressure, namely Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC PTA 5289 (Lr5289), would enable the natural selection of a variant better adapted to such an environment. Using this approach, the novel strain

title: Comparative transcriptional network analysis reveals ecological specialization in infant-associated species of Bifidobacterium.
abstract: Bifidobacterium species are important microorganisms in the infant gut microbiota displaying substantial genomic diversity, yet how this variability is reflected in transcriptional regulatory architecture remains an open question. Here, we integrated pangenome analysis with transcription factor binding site inference and network-based approaches to compare regulatory architectures across Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis, Bifidobacterium breve, and B. longum subsp. longum using over 300 hig

title: Application of IgA-Seq in schizophrenia to identify key gut bacteria that promote abnormal behavior in mice.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) has a complex etiology, and growing evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Because abundance-based profiling does not identify taxa closely engaged by mucosal immunity, we used immunoglobulin A (IgA)-based bacterial sorting to prioritize candidate SCZ-associated gut bacteria and evaluated cultured consortia in mouse models. Fecal samples were collected from participants with SCZ, other mental disorders, and healthy controls, which underwent 16S rRNA gene sequencin

title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on mater

title: Multi-Omics Gut Microbiome Species Communities and Functional Modules Linking Metal Exposures to Children's Neurodevelopmental Health in a Canadian Birth Cohort.
abstract: Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. Here, we integrated stool metal measurements, shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and neurodevelopmental assessments in 116 children aged 8-12 years from the GESTE birth cohort in Sherbrook

title: Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids control cGVHD development by regulating antibody production.
abstract: Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Microbe-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) exert diverse local effects on the intestinal mucosa. We previously reported that a relative deficiency of SCFA in the circulation of transplant patients was associated with an increased incidence of cGVHD. title: Impact of dietary exogenous carbohydrases in combination with sodium butyrate on growth performance, digestive tract health, and welfare aspects of broiler chickens fed with corn or wheat-based diets.
abstract: Exogenous enzymes and sodium butyrate supplementation may effectively alleviate the adverse effects of cereal non starch polysaccharides in broiler diets. Therefore, a total of 400 one-d-old male broiler chicks (ROSS 308) were allocated to a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design to investigate the effects of exogenous carbohydrases (EC, 0 or 100 mg/kg of Natugrain enzyme) and sodium butyrate (SB, 0 or 500 mg/kg) on growth, gizzard development, gut health, and welfare in broilers fed corn or wheat-based die

title: Galactooligosaccharides reshape mucin O-glycosylation and gut microbial metabolism in DSS-challenged piglets.
abstract: The present study examined the effects of dietary galactooligosaccharides (GOS), a food-derived prebiotic carbohydrate, on colonic mucin O-glycosylation and gut microbiota in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-challenged weaned piglets. GOS supplementation reduced diarrhea incidence and colonic mucosal damage while enriching commensal taxa and increasing propionate and butyrate concentrations. LC-MS/MS-based profiling revealed GOS-associated differences in colonic mucin O-glycan features, with putativ

title: Pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes gut microbial metabolic potential and alleviates estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss.
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a bone disease characterized by estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss. Although the gut microbiota has emerged as an important regulator of skeletal homeostasis, it remains unclear whether therapeutic benefits require preservation of the original microbial community. We investigated the effects of pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila (pAkk) in ovariectomized rats. pAkk treatment attenuated trabecular bone loss, suppressed osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, improve

title: Schaftoside, a functional flavonoid from fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.), alleviates depression and cognitive deficits via the microbiome-gut-brain axis in stressed mice.
abstract: Depression involves dysregulation of central and peripheral networks, with gut microbiota alterations increasingly implicated in pathogenesis. Trigonella foenum-graecum L. (fenugreek), a functional food and medicinal herb, has been used traditionally for neurological disorders, yet its specific neuroprotective constituents remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the antidepressant potential of schaftoside, the predominant flavonoid of fenugreek seed flavonoids, and explored its mechani

title: Microbial bile acid deconjugation counters metabolic decline in aging.
abstract: Interventions such as caloric restriction and time-restricted feeding improve lifespan and aging-associated metabolic health, in part through effects on the gut microbiome and bile acid dynamics. However, how aging alters microbial function and bile acid signaling, and whether these changes can be therapeutically leveraged, remain unclear. Here, we show that aged mice exhibit increased deconjugation of taurine-conjugated bile acids accompanied by increased bile salt hydrolase (BSH)-related trans

title: Goat milk fat globule membrane attenuates D-galactose-induced cognitive decline in mice in association with gut microbiota remodeling, increased fecal SCFAs, and GPR41/43-related signaling.
abstract: The global rise in aging-related cognitive decline necessitates effective preventive strategies. The gut microbiota modulates brain function via the microbiota-gut-brain axis, yet the role of goat milk fat globule membrane (GMFGM) in this crosstalk remains to be fully elucidated. This study investigated neuroprotective effects of GMFGM in a D-galactose-induced aging mouse model and examined changes in gut microbiota composition, fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations, and G protein-c

title: Human milk oligosaccharides as immunomodulators of the gut-immune-brain axis: a potential route to suppressing neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common cause of dementia, is characterized by interacting pathological processes in which chronic neuroinflammation plays a central role. The gut-brain axis connects intestinal and central nervous system function through immune, neural, and metabolic pathways, yet how immune signaling integrates these pathways in AD remains unclear. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are structurally diverse bioactive glycans whose immunomodulatory properties extend beyond thei

title: Engineering Microencapsulated Probiotics for Enhanced Aflatoxin M1 Mitigation in Milk.
abstract: Aflatoxin M1 is a major mycotoxin found primarily in milk and dairy products that causes a severe public health risk to dairy product safety and the dairy industry. Therefore, the present study explored the effectiveness of micro-encapsulated Lactobacillus acidophilus, Lactobacillus Casei and Bifidobacterium bifidum in reducing AFM1 in milk as promising and emerging strategies for eliminating and controlling AFM1 in milk. Nonetheless, it is challenging to maintain a high number of live cells in

title: Gut microbiota alterations associated with dietary inflammation and sarcopenia in humans and aged mice: insights from integrated metabolomic analysis.
abstract: Objective: To investigate the association between the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and sarcopenia risk in older adults and identify cross-species microbial signatures linking dietary inflammatory burden with muscle phenotypes. Methods: A total of 1048 older adults were enrolled, and multivariable logistic regression models were applied to evaluate the association between the DII and sarcopenia risk. A sub-cohort of representative participants (n = 86) underwent fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing

title: Gelatinization differentially impacts in vitro fermentation of high-amylose maize starch.
abstract: Some of the starch in a meal, depending on how it was thermally processed, may escape complete digestion in the upper gut and pass into the colon as available for microbial fermentation. This study uses an in vitro batch fecal model to examine the fermentability of high-amylose maize starch (HAMS) that has been gelatinized to different degrees (DG). Compared with native HAMS, more gases and acids were produced from gelatinized HAMS during the initial 4 h of fermentation, which was attributed to

title: Prebiotic effects of lotus seed starch-C18 fatty acid complexes: Role of structural changes during in vitro digestion and fermentation.
abstract: Despite growing interest in starch-lipid complexes as prebiotic ingredients, the impact of fatty acid (FA) unsaturation on their fermentative behavior and gut microbiota modulation remains controversial, largely due to inconsistent structural characterization across studies. Herein, lotus seed starch (LS), notable for its high amylose content, was used to systematically fabricate complexes with C18 FAs of varying unsaturation, such as stearic (SA), oleic (OA), linoleic (LA), and α-linolenic (ALA

title: In vivo pharmacokinetics and lactic acidosis toxicity of Phenformin mediated by gut microbiota in control and pseudo-germ-free rats.
abstract: Phenformin, a classic biguanide, was withdrawn clinically due to severe lactic acidosis, while the non-genetic causes of interindividual toxic susceptibility remain elusive. This study aimed to clarify pharmacokinetics and lactic acidosis toxicity of phenformin mediated by gut microbiota.

title: Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid suppresses osteoclast formation by promoting IL-10+ Breg differentiation via AhR signaling.
abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites play pivotal roles in immune and bone homeostasis; however, the specific metabolites involved in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the role of indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a microbial metabolite of tryptophan, in estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss through integrated microbiome, metabolomic, and immunological analyses. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing combined with targeted metabolomics, we identified

title: Akkermansia muciniphila alleviates osteoporosis by suppressing bone marrow adiposity through the gut microbiota-UDCA-TGR5 axis.
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is characterized not only by progressive bone loss but also frequently by pathological bone marrow adiposity (BMA) expansion. Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK), implicated in lipid metabolic homeostasis, was previously found to be markedly depleted during estrogen deficiency-associated bone loss. However, whether AKK suppresses pathological BMA expansion and the corresponding receptor-mediated mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that AKK significantly attenua

title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA-AhR-GLP-1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)-AhR-GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching Ligilactobacillus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Ses-treated donors partially transferr

title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurot

title: Sodium L-lactate alleviates DSS-induced colitis through gut microbiota remodeling and Akkermansia enrichment.
abstract: L-lactate, a byproduct of glycolysis and hypoxia, accumulates in the gut during disease progression and may affect host responses and microbial metabolism. Here, we investigated the protective effect of sodium L-lactate on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice and the involvement of the gut microbiota. Oral sodium L-lactate significantly alleviated colitis, as shown by reduced body weight loss, fecal occult blood score, colon shortening, and histological injury. It also improved m

title: Prenatal Bifidobacterium bifidum intervention alleviates early-life stress-induced neurobehavioral abnormalities via inhibiting neuroinflammation in offspring mice.
abstract: Early-life stress is a key environmental risk factor for neurobehavioral abnormalities in offspring, which disrupts gut-brain axis homeostasis and causes neurodevelopmental damage. Probiotics have shown important potential in improving neurodevelopmental abnormalities. As a dominant gut microbe in healthy mother-infant pairs, Bifidobacterium bifidum is closely related to neurobehavioral abnormalities. This study aimed to explore the effects of maternal Bifidobacterium bifidum intervention on ear

title: Identification and characterization of polysaccharide from Paeoniae Radix Rubra, and its mechanism in alleviating anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury based on integrating gut microbiota and non-targeted metabolomics.
abstract: A novel polysaccharide, designated PRRP2, was extracted from the dried root of Paeoniae Radix Rubra. Structural analysis suggested that the PRRP2 backbone was predominantly composed of →4)-Glcp-(1→ and →6)-Glcp-(1→ glycosidic linkages, with a trace amount of →2)-Xylp-(1→ embedded within the backbone. journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis

title: Changes in the Cecal Microbiota in a Rat Model of Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease.
abstract: Characteristics of the intestinal microbiota specific to metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) were studied in vivo using male Wistar rats. The consumption of high-fat diets (choline-deficient or cholesterol-supplemented) commonly used in experimental MAFLD models induced shifts in the cecal microbiota. An increase in the number of facultatively anaerobic coccal populations (Enterococcus spp. and Streptococcus spp.) was observed, including potentially pathogenic representatives. The a
journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine

title: Dietary Clostridium butyricum NCU-02 and Its Postbiotic Butyrate Ameliorate Autism Spectrum Disorder-like Symptoms: Involvement of Hippocampal Oxidative Stress Modulation.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition closely linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, yet effective dietary interventions remain limited. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum NCU-02, a probiotic candidate, and its sterile supernatant in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced mouse model of ASD, with emphasis on their postbiotic properties. Both treatments significantly ameliorated core ASD-like behaviors, attenuating

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder.
abstract: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neu

title: Xiao Chai Hu Decoction ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through an Akkermansia muciniphila-associated gut-heart mechanism.
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) induces cardiotoxicity partly through ferroptosis. Xiao Chai Hu Decoction (XCHD) has anti-inflammatory and organ-protective activities, but its effects on DOX-induced cardiac injury and the gut-heart axis remain unclear.

title: Cholecystectomy Remodels Systemic Bile Acid Exposure Without Detectable Changes in Postprandial Response Kinetics.
abstract: Bile acids are cholesterol-derived metabolites that undergo regulated enterohepatic cycling and act as metabolic signalling molecules. Cholecystectomy removes the gallbladder reservoir, but its effects on systemic bile acid exposure and enterohepatic regulation in humans remain incompletely understood. We conducted a prospective paired longitudinal study of 13 adults without known major chronic disease undergoing elective cholecystectomy. Participants underwent standardized mixed-meal testing be

title: Chronic ethanol feeding drives gut microbiome remodeling and influences cholestatic liver injury in mice.
abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of liver-related mortality worldwide and encompasses steatosis, cirrhosis, and alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). AH is frequently accompanied by cholestasis, characterized by impaired bile flow and disrupted bile acid homeostasis. Although gut microbiome (GM) dysbiosis has been linked to ALD progression and cholestatic injury, its functional role in alcohol-associated cholestasis remains unclear. Mice were subjected to chronic ethanol-feed

title: Gut microbiota as a context-dependent modulator of heavy-metal metabolism: Mechanistic analysis and intervention strategies.
abstract: Heavy metal exposure remains a significant environmental health concern; however, the toxicological consequences of microbiota-metal interactions are not uniformly directed. The intestinal microbiota can sequester metals, alter their chemical species, and support barrier and metabolic homeostasis. Conversely, these same processes may also increase solubility or bioaccessibility, generate more reactive intermediates, disrupt bile acid and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) homeostasis, or exacerbate i

title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum postbiotics attenuate Salmonella LPS-triggered neuroinflammation by modulating the microbiota-gut-brain axis in a pig model.
abstract: This study explored the effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (LP) postbiotics on Salmonella LPS-induced neuroinflammation, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms. Sixty pigs were randomly divided into control, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), cell-free supernatant of LP (CFS) and CFS + LPS groups. The pigs were fed with 0.8% CFS or MRS medium for 28 days, and then exposed to 30 μg kg-1 LPS. The results showed that CFS alleviated damage of the liver, colon and brain, and improved brain tight junct

title: Pentadecanoic acid as an emerging microbial-metabolic node for cardiometabolic health.
abstract: The mechanisms underlying the gut microbiota's role in cardiometabolic health remain largely unknown. In a recent article in Nature, Yin et al. identify pentadecanoic acid from Bacteroides uniformis as an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that regulates cholesterol metabolism and atherosclerosis. This work reveals an unrecognized microbial-metabolic axis for cardiometabolic health.
journal: Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM

title: The interplay between gut microbiota and inflammatory markers in bipolar disorder: A systematic review.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis may play a role in the pathophysiology of bipolar disorder (BD), with the gut microbiota influencing immune and inflammatory pathways.

title: Changes in constipation severity and gut microbiota after lactulose administration in patients with chronic constipation: A prospective single-arm interventional study.
abstract: Lactulose is an osmotic laxative that may affect gut microbiota through its prebiotic properties. However, few studies have evaluated the changes in clinical symptoms and gut microbiota before and after lactulose administration in patients with chronic constipation. We aimed to evaluate the changes in constipation symptoms and gut microbiota after 8 weeks of lactulose administration in patients with chronic constipation.

title: Effects of Two Lactobacillus Strains on Aloe Vera-Induced Melanosis Coli in Guinea Pigs and Their Potential Mechanisms.
abstract: This study primarily elucidated the efficacy of Lactobacillus plantarum P-8 (P8) and Lactobacillus acidophilus 85 (LA85) against melanosis coli (MC), a non-inflammatory bowel disease characterized by colonic mucosal lipofuscin deposition, currently lacking specific therapeutic interventions.

title: Advances in research on the gut microbiota-bile acid-immune homeostasis axis in the regulation of bone metabolism in osteoporosis.
abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass, disrupted bone microarchitecture, and an increased risk of fragility fractures. In recent years, the gut microbiota and its metabolites are increasingly recognized as components of an upstream regulatory network linking nutrition, immunity, and bone remodeling. title: Comamonas aquatica diet inhibits TIR-1/SARM1-induced axon degeneration by providing vitamin B12.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests the microbiome critically influences the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases; however, the identity of neuroprotective bacteria and the molecular mechanisms that respond within the host remain largely unknown. Here, we leverage Caenorhabditis elegans' well-characterized nervous system and ability to eat uni-bacterial diets to determine how metabolites and neuroprotective molecules from single species of bacteria suppress degeneration of motor neurons. title: A Biomimetic gut-on-a-chip Integrated with Multi-Omics Reveal the Mechanism of Listeria monocytogenes Infection Microenvironment-Stimulated In Situ Bacteriocin Production by Lactiplantibacillus paraplantarum RX-8.
abstract: Bacteriocins produced in intestine by lactic acid bacteria (LAB) can suppress pathogens and support homeostasis, offering potential against foodborne bacterial infections. However, complex in vivo intestinal milieu hampers monitoring of bacteriocin production and its regulation during enteric infection. Herein, we developed and first applied a three-dimensional gut-on-a-chip with an intact mucus layer, robust barrier function, and stable immune homeostasis to dynamically examine bacteriocin bios

title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum alleviates Parkinson's disease progression by reducing enteroendocrine α-synuclein aggregation in a rotenone-induced mouse model.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder driven by α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation and accumulation. Recent evidence suggests that gut dysbiosis may trigger α-syn accumulation in the enteric nervous system, which spreads to the brain via the vagus nerve. Restoring the gut microbial balance through probiotic intervention offers a promising strategy to mitigate gut-origin pathology in PD. Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PS128 (PS128), a probiotic strain with neuroprotecti

title: Effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 on anxiety, insomnia, and gut microbiota composition in college students.
abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can significantly improve psychiatric symptoms such as insomnia and anxiety via the gut‑brain axis. However, current studies on probiotics for improving insomnia and anxiety in college students remain relatively scarce. In this study, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 was used to evaluate the potential therapeutic effect on insomnia and anxiety in college students by Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA) and Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Subsequently

title: Diet-Driven Modulation of the Gut Microbiome to Enhance Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Cognitive impairment and limited neuroplastic recovery remain major contributors to long-term disability following ischemic stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that stroke-induced disruption of the gut-brain axis, characterized by microbiome dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolite signaling, may influence post-stroke inflammation, synaptic remodeling, and cognitive outcomes. Diet is a key modifiable determinant of gut microbiome composition and metabolic output, yet its role in post-stroke n
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Plasma LBP and sCD14 levels in Parkinson's disease with Asian LRRK2 risk variants: Associations with systemic inflammation and clinical severity.
abstract: LRRK2 is implicated in the Parkinson's disease (PD) microbiome-gut-brain axis. We compared plasma lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) and soluble CD14 (sCD14), markers of gut permeability and endotoxin exposure, in PD patients with/without LRRK2 p.G2385R and/or p.R1628P and controls, and examined their associations with systemic inflammation and clinical severity. title: Complete genome sequence of Bifidobacterium longum BL020 (DSM 33815): a human stool-derived strain from the NORDBIOTIC collection.
abstract: We report the complete genome sequence of Bifidobacterium longum BL020 (DSM 33815), a human stool-derived strain from the NORDBIOTIC collection. The genome consists of a single circular chromosome of 2,413,342 bp with a G + C content of 60.0%.

title: Degradation of mucin O-glycans by a human gut symbiont requires a complex enzyme repertoire and promotes colonization.
abstract: Secreted mucins are the major component of the mucus layer that protects intestinal epithelial surfaces. Mucins are complex glycoproteins decorated with over 100 different O-glycans. Some bacteria degrade mucins, contributing to disruption of the mucus barrier and inflammation. However, the enzymatic pathways by which gut bacteria degrade colonic mucin O-glycans and the impact of this process on gut colonization are unknown. Here, we identified >100 genes that are expressed by the symbiont Bacte

title: Polysaccharide A1 from Bran-Fried Atractylodes lancea Regulates Cyclophosphamide-induced Intestinal Immune Injury in Mice via the Faecalibaculum rodentium-Mediated IAA-AHR/RORC Axis.
abstract: Cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury is often characterized by gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolite imbalance. Bran-fried Atractylodes lancea polysaccharide (FALP-A1) protects against cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury by significantly modulating Faecalibaculum rodentium abundance. However, the mechanism of FALP-A1-mediated F. rodentium regulation remains unclear. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Acetate modulates host physiology and bacterial energetics to improve antibiotic efficacy during obesity-associated infection.
abstract: Antibiotic efficacy is conventionally attributed to the susceptibility of the infecting pathogen. However, obese patients experience disproportionately poor infection outcomes despite receiving antibiotics to which pathogens remain genetically susceptible. These observations suggest that host-associated factors can influence treatment outcomes independently of the bacterial genotype, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using a mechanistic comparison of diet-induced obese

title: l-Arginine Ameliorates IBS-D by Modulating the Ligilactobacillus murinus-LCA-FXR/eNOS Signaling Axis.
abstract: l-Arginine is a semiessential amino acid with diverse metabolic functions and has been implicated in gastrointestinal health through interactions with the gut microbiota; however, its therapeutic potential in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) remains unclear. Here, an IBS-D mouse model was established in C57BL/6J mice, and multiomics analyses combined with in vivo and in vitro validation were performed to investigate the mechanisms underlying l-arginine-mediated protection. l

title: Gut microbiota modulates hyodeoxycholic acid to inhibit leukemia development.
abstract: To explore the role of gut microbiota and bile acid (BA) metabolism in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we analyzed samples from 29 patients via 16S rDNA sequencing and LC-QTOF-MS, and performed functional studies on Enterococcus faecalis and hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA). Results revealed a dynamic shift in gut microbiota diversity during treatment, which recovered after therapy. title: Cadmium sulfide nanoparticles exacerbate colitis via Faecalibaculum rodentium-mediated modulation of the indole-3-lactic acid-Th17 axis.
abstract: With the increasing application of cadmium sulfide nanoparticles (CdS-NPs), their potential adverse effects on intestinal health have attracted growing attention. However, the impact of CdS-NPs exposure on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. title: Indole-3-lactic acid ameliorates thrombocytopenia in primary immune thrombocytopenia by modulating the differentiation of Th17 and Tregs.
abstract: Although some patients with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) benefit from current treatments, there are still some refractory patients. Our previous research showed that the imbalance of the intestinal microbiota is associated with ITP. Indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) may act as a communication channel between the gut microbiota and the immune system. This study aimed to assess the ILA metabolism and the role in ITP. title: Polyamine depletion inhibits murine and human norovirus infection.
abstract: Noroviruses are non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses in the family Caliciviridae. Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. title: Natural Glycosides in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Multi-Target Mechanisms via the Gut-Brain Axis.
abstract: The multifactorial complexity of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, limits the efficacy of single-target therapies. Natural glycosides exhibit promising neuroprotective potential, but their clinical translation is hindered by poor oral bioavailability and limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration. title: Synbiotic of 2'-FL and B. longum subsp. infantis BXY2 Alleviates Colitis in Toddler Microbiota-Associated Mice: Potential Involvement of Gut Microbial Arachidonic Acid Metabolism.
abstract: Increasing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence in toddlers requires safe interventions. We developed a synbiotic combining 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) with Bifidobacterium strain and evaluated its protective efficacy against DSS-induced colitis in toddler microbiota-associated (TMA) mice. Among 30 Bifidobacterium strains, Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis BXY2 and Bifidobacterium. breve BG4 utilized 2'-FL in vitro. title: Hyaluronic acid-grafted pH-responsive microcarriers for CD44-targeted co-delivery of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and its extrusion-derived bacterial membrane vesicles to rebalance intestinal homeostasis.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) stems from gut dysbiosis, impaired intestinal epithelial barriers and persistent mucosal immune dysfunction. Free oral probiotics or probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles yield poor therapeutic effects against IBD, as they degrade rapidly in the gastrointestinal tract and lack specific tropism for inflamed colon lesions. title: Azelaic Acid Mediates the Protective Effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m against Colitis via PPARγ Activation.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a high recurrence risk. Although probiotics show promise for UC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Herein, we found that Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m, isolated from yak yogurt, alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice, improving symptoms, restoring intestinal barrier function, and alleviating gut microbiota dysbiosis. title: A core genome multilocus sequence typing scheme for Bacteroides fragilis: insights into population structure and genomic epidemiology.
abstract: Bacteroides fragilis strains are important members of the human gut microbiota and represent major opportunistic pathogens responsible for a wide range of anaerobic infections. Their clinical relevance is reinforced by diverse antimicrobial resistance mechanisms and a complex population structure comprising two major phylogenetic lineages, Division I and Division II. title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3.
abstract: The gut microbiota programs mammalian circadian metabolism, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. Because feeding behavior is inherently rhythmic and strongly influences microbial metabolism, we hypothesized that the microbiota translates feeding timing into host circadian programs. We show that gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (Bt), in concert with feeding schedules, promotes diurnal chromatin-binding activity of the histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) in intestinal epithelial cells. title: Dietary pectin remodels commensal bacterial surfaces to promote IgA-mediated protection from intestinal inflammation.
abstract: Diet-microbe interactions shape mucosal immunity, yet how dietary cues drive strain-specific immunoglobulin A (IgA) responses remains poorly understood. Here, we show that dietary pectin induces a microbiota-dependent high-IgA phenotype in gnotobiotic mice mono-colonized with Bacteroides uniformis (B. uniformis). title: Functional methylthio-alkane reductases are widely distributed for bacterial organic sulfur acquisition.
abstract: Methylthio-alkane reductase (MAR) is a relative of nitrogenase that cleaves methylthio-alkanes for methanethiol liberation and subsequent methionine biogenesis. For example, dimethylsulfide, the most abundant volatile organic sulfur compound, is cleaved to methanethiol and methane. To date, the only verified MAR enzymes are from Alphaproteobacteria like Rhodospirillum rubrum, despite the long-time observation of gene homologs with potential MAR function present across diverse taxa. title: A commensal-derived sugar protects against obesity by regulating immunometabolism.
abstract: Obesity is a worsening global epidemic that is partially regulated by the microbiota through unknown factors. We discovered a human commensal bacterium, Clostridium immunis, which prevents and treats obesity in mice by secreting a phosphocholine-modified exopolysaccharide. Loss- and gain-of-function bacterial mutants involving the phosphocholine biosynthesis locus (licABC) revealed that the phosphocholine moiety is required to protect against metabolic disease. title: A gut mucin muncher signals protection in the uterus.
abstract: Microbial communities occupy distinct anatomical niches, yet their byproducts can influence distant tissues. In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Qu et al. link the gut bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila to tyrosol production. In a mouse model, tyrosol reaches the uterus and protects against endometritis, inflammation of the uterine lining.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
abstract: Approximately 85% of colorectal cancers (CRCs) are microsatellite stable (MSS) and thus exhibit intrinsic resistance to anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) therapy. In this study, we demonstrate that oral administration of Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk) suppresses tumorigenesis and reprograms the tumor microenvironment in MSS CRC mouse models. title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects against endometritis through a tyrosol-mediated gut-uterus axis.
abstract: Endometritis is a common reproductive disorder in humans and domestic animals that causes infertility and livestock losses. However, few specific bacteria and related metabolites involved in its pathogenesis have been identified. Here, we find that endometritis cows (EC) exhibit gut dysbiosis, with depletion of Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK). Gut microbiota transplantation from EC (E-GMT) induces endometritis in mice, whereas gut microbiota transplantation from healthy cows (H-GMT) does not. Supp

title: Dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain axis induced by intermittent access to palatable food is associated with binge-like eating regardless of obesity development.
abstract: Recurrent consumption of energy dense palatable foods contributes to the rising prevalence of obesity and can also promote loss-of-control eating in a subset of individuals. Obesity is commonly associated with peripheral inflammation, impaired sensitivity to appetite-regulating hormones, and alterations in gut microbiota composition, all of which may exacerbate binge-eating behaviors. title: The gut microbiome is associated with structural and functional brain alterations in adolescents with social anxiety disorder.
abstract: Social anxiety disorder (SAD) commonly emerges in childhood or early adolescence and is associated with persistent impairments in social and emotional functioning. Although structural and functional brain abnormalities have been reported in SAD, the potential involvement of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in adolescent SAD remains poorly understood.

title: Bacteroidetes promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and resistance to immunotherapy.
abstract: Growing evidence highlights the gut microbiome's critical role in tumorigenesis and immunotherapy response. However, the impact of gut microbes on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains unclear due to the lack of combined preclinical and clinical studies.

title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. Using aged laying hens, a livestock model with a relatively short digestive tract, we examined the gut microbiota, faecal metabolome, and breast-muscle metabolome by integrative multi-omics analyses in hens fed a Caldifermentibacillus hisashii-containing fermented feed or a control diet. title: Microbiome-derived bile acids contribute to elevated antigenic response and bone erosion in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. It has been widely recognized that gut microbial dysbiosis is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of RA, although distinct alterations in microbiota have been associated with this disease. Yet, the metabolites that mediate the impacts of the gut microbiome on RA are less well understood. title: An iron acquisition system promotes Bifidobacterium longum fitness in competitive early life gut communities
abstract: Iron availability influences the composition of the gut microbiota, yet the mechanisms that enable beneficial bacteria to acquire iron and compete within iron-variable communities remain poorly understood. Here, we identify Fei (Fe import), an iron-responsive acquisition system that promotes the fitness of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. longum, a prevalent member of the early-life gut microbiota. title: Formate, hydrogen, and acetate shape the morphology, physiology and lifestyles of the host-associated methanogen Methanobrevibacter smithii
abstract: Methane-producing archaea (methanogens) are increasingly linked to gastrointestinal, neuropsychiatric, and neurodevelopmental disorders. These conditions are often associated with altered microbial metabolism that changes the availability of acetate, formate, hydrogen, carbon dioxide, and methane in the gut.
